## Current reviewed candidate

Published head: `6186416ddd83c365405a798130999cb1e4df0f31`  
Reviewed local composition: `a5fcf75578a26beddce6e8b9110e1c8924bafdd2`  
Exact shared whole tree: `f611a03c49b5862052271789e9b353e09ecbb7da`

## Completed-main baseline restoration

The preceding analytics Core run exposed inherited notification-erasure and G703 scanner findings. All ten affected owned candidates contained the same older source. After a fresh 38-PR and 59-worktree ownership survey, this update restores exactly four bounded paths from completed accepted-main work:

- Resource-linked notification-body redaction from main ancestor `28326597340a4f0efad33f37feecc380db0de66f`.
- The accepted resource-relation regression, retaining unrelated/same-name, exact-link, prefix and cross-network controls.
- The deterministic erasure fixture and credential invariants from accepted ancestor `fc31dc9a6b8c102fe612f47bc543e94e8114df0f`.
- Only the two existing operator-path G703 annotation comments in `writeAtomicPrivateFile`; its executable body and the remainder of the older util file are unchanged. No broad scanner suppression or configuration change is introduced.

All other paths, every future-module subtree, root dependencies, workflows and feature flags remain unchanged. The module stays disabled and on integration **HOLD**.

## Actual verification and limits

The same accepted tests genuinely fail with the old SQL and pass with the restored SQL. On representative `6dce81719ab44e20256e1767f3cc3d5c73b89961`, the selected actual-Core-SQLite race run passed in **33.160s wall**, focused service/store vet in **119.240s**, and module verification in **7.049s**. Formatting and whitespace checks pass. The pinned Core driver graph is unchanged, including SQLite1.60.1, libc1.79.0 and x/sys0.49.0.

This candidate matches all 440 captured representative Core inputs; independent comparison also verifies the complete internal subtree, embedded data, root module and checksum files. The focused run was executed once on the representative, not separately on every PR.

Two independent reviews verified the source, original failures, unchanged test bytes, raw-log hashes and all composed trees. Remote commit/tree/ordered-parent and four-path blob readbacks match the frozen local compositions.

These focused results do not replace current-head full Core, lint, native module or ordinary approval gates. Native module successes on preceding module-identical heads remain dated evidence. The older baseline has no configured traceability generator/Make/CI gate; its handmade matrix is unchanged and no absent check is claimed as a pass. Core #104 has its own separate generated-traceability handoff.

Complete evidence and current ownership: [master consolidation #104](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/circula/pull/104). The source-specific earlier record is retained below; identities in this section are current.

<details>
<summary>Earlier module work and qualification record</summary>

## Why

The advertised receipts branch lacks later source recovered from the verified archive. Reviewing that implementation also exposed a plain offline-parser defect: JCS converted raw numbers to IEEE-754 before integer validation, allowing some fractional or underflowed values to become accepted integers.

## Recovery and repair

Restore saved head `91529c5a3a4268ecf3a919e099ab9aca779aab2d` onto its published ancestor `bd2fbdbd3adf77b27fa12335ff2827359423aea3`. All44 original files are retained,42 byte-identical. All6 original test files, both pinned dependency files and the disabled/HOLD manifest are unchanged. The two changed original files are the current README and the reviewed `canonical.go` repair; one numeric regression file is added.

Recovered functionality includes authorized ephemeral TXT/JSON/print receipts, exact bounded integer projections, strict offline canonical parsing, an optional consented standard JWS/EdDSA certificate candidate, local trust/key lifecycle checks, and no-JS HTTP/CLI seams. This does not enable the module or adopt production signing/key-custody policy.

The decoder now compares original amount/revision/precision tokens exactly with their already validated integer DTO. Bounded digit/exponent comparison preserves integral decimal/exponent spellings and signed zero without arbitrary-size arithmetic. The certificate issuer/verifier and wire profile are unchanged. The finding is unsigned offline parsing integrity; no signature forgery or authorization bypass is claimed.

## Source and independent review

Published head: `4f04285a1fb7141a27acd37aab3b7185cc177534`.
Reviewed local composition: `d7578baf80a613b378812889478166b45fc91636` (workflow-only follow-up to the fully tested runtime composition `3466df2fe5a73de17e25c5a68315eead0e3ac926`).
Exact full-tree equality: `58b569a0ba1016737d5c575044a8d9dcc5c8f442`.

The original archive/restoration/workflow and final15-path documentation follow-up were independently reviewed. The numeric repair authored separately at `abaa1e8942f0997f86ce9e3bbc6d80b2dd65d056` received independent root review. Both reviewed Go blobs exactly match this candidate. All63 published path blobs were verified.

Outside the module and its new dedicated workflow, exactly two files are restored to their already-merged main blobs: the missing audit-anchor `os` import and the departure regression fixture cap. Production limits remain unchanged. Their accepted-main provenance is recorded; no unfinished active-worker source, root dependencies, shared CI or migrations are copied.

## Actual qualification

- Unchanged-source regression:11 fractional/underflow subcases failed as expected because the old decoder accepted them;18 exact boundary/representation controls already passed.
- Repaired complete module ordinary tests: PASS,84.6% coverage,0.044s package time /5.148s wall.
- Repaired vet: PASS,13.845s wall; module verification and formatting PASS.
- Original unchanged archive race suite: PASS,84.1% coverage,87 pass events/no skips. This is preserved as historical source-specific evidence, not claimed for the new numeric repair.
- Current repaired source full race: PASS,40 top-level tests /118 pass events,zero skips,84.6% coverage,1.279s package /5.349s wall. All three100,000-execution fuzz campaigns passed: CreateReceipt66.539s, DecodeDocument13.546s and VerifyCertificate11.422s wall. Every source/dependency hash stayed unchanged. These results qualify the exact runtime/test/dependency bytes preserved by the workflow-only follow-up. The new provider workflow requests native Linux/macOS race and Windows ordinary tests; those current-head provider gates remain separate.

See `future/receipts/RECOVERY-20261119.md` and `recovery-evidence-20261119/` for exact commands, original failures, source hashes and independent reviews.

## Native workflow guard correction

The preceding exact head `3cc55f79` failed the isolation guard on all three native jobs in [run 44531463364](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/circula/actions/runs/44531463364), before tests ran. Go-generated test package names (`owned.test` and `owned [owned.test]`) did not satisfy the workflow's package-name predicate.

The independently reviewed follow-up changes only `.github/workflows/future-receipts.yml` (three insertions/two deletions). It checks actual owning `Module.Path` values against the receipts module and the two existing pinned dependencies. Manifest, dependency, test and native execution requirements are preserved; Core and other future-module imports remain rejected.

The unchanged original guard fails locally on actual dependency output; the corrected guard passes Linux and Windows/Darwin-target dependency listings. Negative Core and areas module controls both fail as required. Independent review verifies all six receipts/logs, unchanged module hashes and workflow syntax. Cross-target dependency listing is not native test execution. The new published head requires fresh native/Core results; the original three provider failures remain preserved.

## Merge and feature boundary

Keep this draft until the actual current head passes all applicable module/Core, native, browser, lint/vulnerability, build, fuzz, reproducibility and ordinary review requirements. It targets only the original isolated receipts branch.

Whole-verifier interoperability, actual Core read-transaction/auth/key adapters, production trust distribution and cryptographic operations, manual browser/accessibility acceptance and explicit later integration selection remain open. The feature stays disabled/HOLD. No Core activation, release or deployment is included.

</details>

## Problem and resulting behavior

Pending camera permission, playback, scanner imports and decode results could outlive Stop, page exit, document hiding or a newer operation. A late result could reopen capture or overwrite the manual input and submit an obsolete preview. Independent review also reproduced stale completion after an oversized replacement image and after a manual form submission.

The wrapper now ties every asynchronous completion to its current visible operation. Cancellation immediately stops attached media. Each bundled Nimiq scanner owns a separate video element, so its delayed cleanup cannot stop a newer camera stream. New file selection and actual form submission invalidate previous work. Existing successful native/fallback previews and a file event with no new selection retain their behavior.

## Scope and provenance

This is a selective adaptation of recovered camera-lifecycle ideas to the current QR implementation; it does not replace the service, API, persistence or scanner library.

- QR scanner and worker distributions, module Go source, dependencies, routes and disabled/HOLD manifest remain unchanged.
- A separate Node-only workflow qualifies the lifecycle suite on native Linux, macOS and Windows.
- Exactly two already-accepted main files restore the inherited missing `os` import and the departure test's fixture cap. Both exact blobs and their accepted-main introducing commits are documented; no production cap or unfinished worker source changes.

Reviewed local head: `3c1ce7a7dc190271a9a830abc924f4f938049801`

Exact shared whole tree: `6c5f55e7fe658d5144c3c09c010f74923397c7df`  
Isolated target/base: `future/fux-102-qr-20261116` at `9db8a323d7dcf430d1a58a4a4d10ca3628aeb401`

The complete six-path candidate and accepted-main follow-up received independent source review. The source script, lifecycle tests and dedicated workflow retain the exact blobs qualified at `7a33e6e1ce18c04f0b0713a4895934f547e45bb9`.

## Observed verification

The unchanged initial application failed 21 of 23 lifecycle tests; the normal preview and unsupported-camera controls passed. The first repair passed all 23. Independent review then added four cases: the same expanded suite passed 24 and failed three stale-result regressions before the final repair, then passed **27/27 with zero skips** afterwards.

An independent root rerun also passed all 27 cases and both script syntax checks. A separate reviewer replayed the two originally reported cancellation probes against final source: **2/2 passed**. Two suite cases evaluate the exact bundled Nimiq lifecycle implementation. Action pins, YAML, the disabled module boundary, source scope and whitespace were checked.

**Current-head native/provider results are pending.** These are deterministic DOM/media/decoder tests, not real mobile camera, browser/CSP, accessibility, session or ledger integration acceptance. No payment or authorization bypass is claimed from the preview-navigation defect.

The module remains disabled and on integration HOLD. Normal current-head checks and review requirements apply before merging into the isolated QR target.


</details>
